classification.difficultyReason: Read matching length marks to establish both outer right triangles, calculate their internal hypotenuses, then use those as legs of the central right triangle. The dependency chain follows the taught intermediate-length approach.

content.prompt: Determine the unknown value, give your answer in exact form.

spec.description: Schematic right-angled triangle with an internal segment and external capped dimensions.
spec.mathematics: The outer triangle has perpendicular sides consisting of height 75 and a total base of a+12, with hypotenuse 125. The internal segment joins the top vertex to the base division point. Its length is not supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the unknown a are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ be the entire base length.
$$\begin{align*}L&=\sqrt{125^2-75^2}\\L&=100\\a&=100-12\\a&=88\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: All diagram lengths are in centimetres.

spec.description: Three connected right-angled triangles with two distinct equal-length tick families.
spec.mathematics: The left height and right base segment are both 8. The left base segment and right height are both 15. Each internal sloping segment has length 17; they are perpendicular at the base division point. The upper edge a is their hypotenuse.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 8 and 15, equality marks, three right-angle marks and unknown a are visible.

answer.worked:
The equal-length marks give a right base segment of $8\text{ cm}$ and a right vertical side of $15\text{ cm}$. Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be the two internal sloping lengths, measured in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}d_1&=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}\\d_1&=17\\d_2&=\sqrt{15^2+8^2}\\d_2&=17\\a&=\sqrt{17^2+17^2}\\a&=\sqrt{578}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
